conventions: (v1) C-pairing: prices paired by amount and percent, then by evidence overlap, then by field agreement (global greedy); one quicksprout pair that joined two different occurrences was split.

(v1) C-included: 'included' holds the allowances or inclusions stated with that occurrence (users, projects, storage, data, devices, minutes, nights, items said to be included), not feature descriptions, delivery formats or 'recommended for' lines.

(v1) C-included-bought: the quantity being bought is not repeated in 'included' when it is already in the product name or in basis_quantity; a variant size goes to 'included' only when the product name lacks it.

(v1) C-included-conditions: wallet top-up / spend thresholds and validity periods are purchase conditions (included null); a volume tier tied to a per-unit rate ('for a quantity of 5000-10,000 SMS') is kept in 'included' as written.
(v1) C-basis-vocab: basis uses the guide's singular generic unit: 'message' for SMS and SMS units.
(v1) C-goods-basis: goods sold as a whole item or pack with no 'per' wording have basis and basis_quantity null; a basis is set only when the text states a per-unit (/kg, /lb, / bunch, /pc).

(v1) C-names: plan and product as the page writes them at that occurrence (row or column label, heading incl. its descriptor), without footnote markers or embedded prices; an allowance in parentheses goes to 'included'.

(v1) C-plan-vs-product: on a vendor's own page separate services are 'product' (plan null) and tiers are 'plan'; on review, comparison and news pages 'product' is the tool or company priced and its tier or service line is 'plan'.
(v1) C-product-qualifier: qualifiers of a basis or ticket (employee type, card type, one-way/return, passenger row) are neither product nor plan; they stay in the evidence.
(v1) C-addon-name: an add-on's product is the add-on's name as written.

(v1) C-tax-scope: tax comes from a statement that covers the price: page-level ('All prices ...', an unscoped '* GST will be charged in addition to mentioned prices', a tax FAQ on fees) applies page-wide; a statement naming one kind of price (MRP) applies only to it; otherwise null.
(v1) C-effective-scope: an article-level 'Prices as of' / 'Sources checked on' date applies to every price in the article.
(v1) C-billed-scope: a billing commitment stated in an FAQ block ('We only offer annual billing') applies to the prices in that block.
(v1) C-period: period only when stated with the amount (incl. 'month-to-month' and a JSON-LD offer's own description); a 'Monthly/Annual billing' row label sets billed, not period.

(v1) C-promo: promotional true only on visible evidence (struck/was price, a stated discount, promo or first-term framing); a CSS class or a conflicting figure elsewhere is not evidence, and false is then judgeable.
(v1) C-same-offer: repeats of one offer (JSON-LD copy, variant option, per-unit breakdown of a discounted price) carry that offer's stated promotional and tax properties.
(v1) C-currency: a bare $ is read as the currency the page itself writes for the same shop's prices ('$9.99 AUD', JSON-LD AUD).
(v1) C-attribution: 'none' when no plan or product name exists (tiers named by size, page-wide fees); 'clear' when the product is plain even if the plan is unnamed.

(v1) C-unjudgeable: a field is unjudgeable only when the snapshot cannot settle it (toggle state not in HTML, nature of a trial-period price); a field the guide nulls when unstated (period) is not unjudgeable.
(v1) C-paise: fast2sms '0.25 paisa' read as INR 0.25 (the page's own tier lists give Rs 0.25/SMS for the same two offers, in a 'highest price' section); all other paise converted as written.
(v1) C-illustrative: a generic illustrative example naming no product ('a plan advertised around $3/month ... renew at $10-$18/month') is a not-price (other).
(v1) C-approx: 'around the low-$3s' is kept as a price with amount 3, bound about.
(v1) C-conflicts-as-written: contradictory figures on one page (instamojo cards vs table, neworg JSON-LD vs visible text, fast2sms Rs 60,000 vs 600000) are all labelled as written.

(v1) C-np-merge: not-prices are the union of A and B, merged when amounts match and one evidence contains the other (longer evidence kept); why: 'save X' = savings, 'X% off' = discount, other non-fee percentages = percentage_not_fee, a bundled benefit's worth or another party's price = other.
(v1) C-layout: layout is not compared by agree.py; A's value kept where they differ.

C-pairing-v2 (new in v2): pairs by amount and percent, then evidence similarity, then field agreement (global greedy); gives agree.py's 543 pairs, 5 only-A, 53 only-B. 'unjudgeable' differences are adjudicated as a field too.
C-template (new in v2): <template> content is inert and not rendered, so it is not visible text and is not labelled (sumup_gb variant cards/FAQs).
C-hidden-data (new in v2): amounts only in data attributes (toggle alternates: pilot quarterly CFO prices, syn2_insurance_de yearly premiums) are not visible and not labelled.

C-bare-dollar-local (new in v2): bare $ on a page about Mexico, New Zealand or Canada with no code written is currency null, not assumed USD (smartfit_mx, syn2_farmshop_nz, canadapost_rates), per the guide.

C-toggle-state (new in v2): when the HTML carries the toggle's selected state (switch__opt--on; annual values with 'billed annually' shown), billed follows it and is judgeable; a prepaid commitment whose cycle length is not stated ('Pagamento integral e antecipado') makes billed unjudgeable.
C-currency-null (new in v2): a quote or a percentage has currency null and currency_assumed false; JSON-LD priceCurrency means not assumed.
C-quote-fields (new in v2): a quote has no amount, so page-wide tax statements are not applied to it (tax null) and eligibility thresholds are not 'included'.

C-basis-stated (new in v2): basis only when the page writes what the amount is per ('per ticket', 'por caso', '/stamp', 'Price for 5 terabytes'); a fee caption or pricing_type alone does not set it, and a percentage's base ('of the estate value', 'of your credit') is not a basis.

C-fee-label (new in v2): a separately listed fee or service line on the vendor's own page takes its own label as product, as written (booking fee, Gastos de gestion, Cuota de inscripcion, Afiliacion, Contracargo, Delivery, Egress & API fees), attribution clear; the 'Transaction fee' caption of a plan card's headline rate is not a product.
C-aggregate-offer (new in v2): a JSON-LD AggregateOffer low/high is a range over the offers; plan null, product the enclosing JSON-LD item's name when it has one (clear), else attribution none.

C-names-v2 (new in v2): plan/product names are taken verbatim at the occurrence, including JSON-LD Offer names ('CFO Basic', 'Holded Plus'), card headings ('For C-Corps', 'Free for free'), tab labels ('Canada stamp rates', 'CFO') and FAQ spelling ('pay as you go'); a '/ month' unit in a column header is the period, not part of the name.
C-worth (new in v2): 'worth GBP X' next to a listed service (crunch quote builder) gives a value, not a price charged; not-price (other), as v1's bundled-benefit rule.
C-market-average (new in v2): averages of insurers' premiums by breed (quotezone_pet table and its FAQPage JSON-LD copy) are not an offer's price: not-price (competitor_average).
C-gift-card (new in v2): a gift card sold in a shop is a not-price (gift_card), as the guide lists gift cards.

C-cta (new in v2): navigation or advice lines about getting quotes ('Get an instant quote in minutes', 'It's best to get personalised quotes') are not quote prices; a stated quote-only case (FAQ 'they can provide you a quote' for >5,000 free tickets, 'On request' cells) is.

C-illustrative-v2 (new in v2): calculator outputs marked illustrative (tickettailor 'Payment processing fees*: GBP 0.40') are not-prices (other); JS-placeholder calculator outputs stay prices with unjudgeable ['*'] (v2 labelling note).
C-np-why (new in v2): a weight or size limit is 'other', not 'count'; a refundable deposit is 'other'.
